spec.description: Storage capacity and growth forecasting for Proxmox datastores, plus health of the telemetry pipeline itself (ingest freshness and OpenTelemetry Collector throughput).

spec.title: Total Capacity
spec.description: Sum across selected storages. Shared storages are counted once per node that sees them, so this can overcount in a cluster.

spec.title: Inactive
spec.description: Storages that are configured and enabled but not currently active -- an unmounted NFS/CIFS share, or an unreachable PBS. Zero is emitted only when storage source metrics exist.

spec.expr: count(proxmox_storage_enabled{node=~"$node", storage=~"$storage"} == 1 and proxmox_storage_active{node=~"$node", storage=~"$storage"} == 0) or (count(proxmox_storage_enabled{node=~"$node", storage=~"$storage"}) * 0)
sum by (storage, node) (proxmox_storage_used{node=~"$node", storage=~"$storage"} / proxmox_storage_total{node=~"$node", storage=~"$storage"})

spec.title: Storage Availability
spec.description: Whether each storage was ACTIVE, sampled over time. A network-backed store (NFS, CIFS, iSCSI) that drops out stops updating its capacity figures, and every capacity panel then shows a flat line that is indistinguishable from a storage nobody is writing to. This is the panel that tells the two apart. `enabled` is the administrative setting and lives in the detail table; `active` is the runtime truth.

spec.title: Growth Rate
spec.description: Storage growth rate from a 6-hour least-squares fit. Positive means filling; negative means space is being freed.

spec.title: Time to Full
spec.description: Days until each storage fills at its current 6-hour trend. Storages that are shrinking or flat are excluded by the `> 0` guard and show as 'stable' -- a projection off a negative slope is meaningless, not infinite.

options.content: Proxmox emits **no `up{}` metric**, so pipeline health has to be derived from the data itself: how long ago the newest sample landed, and how many samples arrived per hour. Expected cadence is **120/hour** (Proxmox pushes every ~10s, VictoriaMetrics deduplicates to 30s).

spec.title: Ingest Age
spec.description: Seconds since the newest Proxmox sample. Over 90s means something in the chain stopped.

spec.title: Samples / hour
spec.description: Per series. Well below 120 means pushes are being dropped or the collector is restarting.

spec.title: Series Count by Family
spec.description: Cardinality by area. A sudden drop means guests stopped; a sudden jump usually means a new guest or disk. blockstat dominates -- it is one metric per virtual disk per field.

spec.title: Node Inventory
spec.description: Every node reporting, with the PVE version it identifies as.

options.content: These panels read the OpenTelemetry Collector's **own** telemetry from its `:8888` endpoint, which is a separate scrape target from the Proxmox metrics. Process and queue metrics exist at startup; receiver and batch metrics are created only after the first OTLP request. If every panel is empty, check the self-telemetry scrape — see `docs/configuration.md`.

spec.title: Metric Points Through the Collector
spec.description: Accepted should track sent. Any sustained refused/failed means Proxmox data is being dropped. Note these are receiver-side counters: the exporter's send_failed counter is created lazily by the collector and does not exist until the first failure, so it cannot be charted pre-emptively -- watch the export queue instead.

spec.title: Export Queue
spec.description: A queue that climbs toward capacity means the backend cannot keep up; once full, data is dropped.

spec.title: Collector Uptime
spec.description: Resets to zero on every restart. Frequent resets point at OOM or a config reload loop.

spec.title: Batch Send Size
spec.description: Metric points per exported batch. Batches pinned at the configured maximum mean the collector is saturating its send path.
